Date: Tue, 20 Jan 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Pen Test timeline & vulnerability management next steps

Thanks again for the call this morning — great discussion and appreciate the clear security priorities. Quick recap and proposed next steps on our side so we can keep momentum: 

Summary of what we covered:
- HealthBridge is evaluating Redwood for HIPAA-bearing workloads and wants assurance around pen testing, remediation SLAs, and data protection controls (SOC 2, encryption, logging).
- You asked for a recent pen test summary (redacted) and our typical vulnerability SLA/cadence.
- You also prefer we start a vendor security questionnaire in your portal and execute an NDA before sharing full reports.

Proposed next steps (please confirm):
1) I will share our SOC 2 Type II report and a redacted pen-test summary today (attached).
2) Mina (security) will send our vulnerability management SLA and cadence; she'll also outline how we handle critical findings and patch windows.
3) Rafael/Sean to coordinate any product/architecture follow-ups.
4) Marissa to send NDA link & start questionnaire flow once you confirm the preferred portal.

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2025.pdf (summary), Vuln_SLA_Draft.xlsx (draft SLA & cadence).

If that matches your expectations, I can kick off the NDA and questionnaire tomorrow and we can schedule a 30-minute follow-up to finalize pen-test scope.

Best,
Marissa Cole

From: Paul Lin <paul.lin@healthbridge.com>

Cc: Dana Kwon <dana.kwon@healthbridge.com>, security@healthbridge.com
Date: Tue, 20 Jan 2026 13:45:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Pen Test timeline & vulnerability management next steps

Thanks Marissa — that plan looks good. A few clarifying questions from our side before we move to NDA: 

1) Scope: We need confirmation the pen test covers internet-facing endpoints and the inference API layer (not only internal infra). If there are agent/edge components, note those too.
2) HIPAA: Can you confirm whether you have a HIPAA controls mapping (we need confirmation of encryption-in-transit/rest, access logging, BAA status).
3) Previous pen test report: can you share a redacted full pen-test report (high/critical findings and remediation notes) under NDA? We do need to review remediation timetables.
4) SLA asks: For our procurement team — what is your target SLA for remediation of critical/high vulnerabilities? Is there an acknowledgement SLA and a remediation timeline?

Prefer to have the vendor questionnaire initiated via our portal (security.healthbridge.com/vendor-portal). Who should I expect to be the primary point of contact to fill that out?

Appreciate the quick turnaround here — aiming to complete security review within the next 3 weeks.

— Paul
Paul Lin
Senior Security Engineer | HealthBridge Inc
paul.lin@healthbridge.com
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Paul Lin <paul.lin@healthbridge.com>, Dana Kwon <dana.kwon@healthbridge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jan 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pen Test timeline & vulnerability management next steps

Hi Paul — copying answers inline and attaching a redacted pen-test summary as requested.

1) Scope: Yes — we will include external (internet-facing) endpoints and the public inference API endpoints in scope. If you want TLS termination or private connectors tested, confirm and we'll add. No customer-side agents are required for core hosted API testing.

2) HIPAA: We have a HIPAA controls mapping and are willing to share the control matrix under NDA. In short:
- Encryption: TLS 1.2+/AES-256 at rest for customer data stores, in-transit TLS for API.
- Logging: Request/response logging with RBAC access; audit logs retained according to contract (can be adjusted).
- BAA: We provide a BAA for enterprise customers; draft BAA can be provided with NDA.

3) Pen test report: We can provide a redacted summary (attached: PenTest_Redacted_Summary.pdf). For the full report, we require an executed NDA — we can route DocuSign.

4) Vulnerability SLAs & cadence: typical operating model (we can adjust per contract):
- Scanning cadence: weekly authenticated scans for infra components + daily alerting for critical CVEs (automated).
- Pen testing cadence: annual full pen-test with additional targeted tests after major releases/feature launches.
- Acknowledgement SLA: critical findings — acknowledgement within 48 hours.
- Remediation target: critical — mitigation plan within 7 days and patch/mitigation implemented within 30 days where possible; exceptions handled via agreed remediation plan with dates.
- Disclosure: We provide redacted finding summaries to customers; full findings are shared post-NDA and on a need-to-know basis (we do not publish full vendor reports).

Attachments included: PenTest_Redacted_Summary.pdf, Vuln_SLA_Draft.xlsx.

If you want different SLA windows, we can put options in the contract (e.g., 14-day remediation for non-critical, 72-hour patch for critical for Dedicated customers).

Regards,
Mina Haddad
Head of Security | Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com
From: Paul Lin <paul.lin@healthbridge.com>

Subject: Re: Pen Test timeline & vulnerability management next steps

Thanks Mina — that's helpful. A couple follow-ups: 

- NDA: we'll need an executed NDA before we can accept the full report. Can you send your standard NDA (DocuSign preferred)?
- Questionnaire: please start the vendor questionnaire in our portal (security.healthbridge.com/vendor-portal). We generally require the vendor to initiate and grant us an editor account. If that's not possible, we can accept a completed exported questionnaire.
- SLA: the 48-hour acknowledgement and 7-day mitigation plan sound reasonable; procurement will want a binding remediation timeline for criticals (we'll flag any deviations during SOW).

Please route the NDA to dana.kwon@healthbridge.com (legal) and paul.lin@healthbridge.com (security). Once NDA is in place we'll request full report access.

— Paul
